unresolved_questions: Did a useful feasible noninitialization plan exist before the return budget?
Were useful lower-objective historical iterates rejected for numerical violations?
What changes under a same-state common-seed comparison?
Does a targeted revision improve measured closed-loop behavior?
lessons: Synchronous simulation latency does not imply missed virtual-time actions.
Numerical feasibility does not establish task success.
Selected initialization is distinct from exception fallback.
Missing historical traces cannot establish why an unseen iterate was rejected.
A successful local comparison does not establish closed-loop improvement.
Another stopping condition ending a 30s-budget solve does not establish that extending the return budget is ineffective.
applicability_limits: One frozen simulated structure/task/controller; no unique cause, hardware result or global conclusion.
